description: During defk-jaj, fuzzy_search verify measured defk ~27-28 ms vs ~21 ms for the blocking (yield: false) version, on both main and the branch, on a heavily loaded machine (load avg 30+). The defk-nua README note records 20 ms yielding vs 20 ms yield: false. Either load noise or an earlier regression (candidates: defk-5s3 flat-loop safepoints, defk-j3h 250us slice, defk-jp3/7q5 selects, defk-jaj inlining + DEFK_STRIP 512->2048). Done when re-measured on a quiet machine; if the gap is real, bisect to the commit and fix or document.

comments.text: From defk-8i4 (DP+early cutoff in both backends, provisional busy-machine numbers): elixir 112→60 ms/query, defk 20.6→14.1, blocking 20.6→13.4. Quiet re-measure should also: re-run loadgen (README under-load table predates the cutoff), and check the yielding-vs-blocking cost, which moved from -2% to +4.7-4.9% (~55 yields/query). See also defk-l2g (Myers in plain Elixir ~18 ms).

Quiet re-measure 2026-10-13 (load 3-6, no builds; 8dfe357). verify.exs x5: elixir 59.9-61.4, defk 13.6-13.8, blocking 13.1-13.3 ms -> 4.4x. yield_cost x5: +3.5-4.5% at ~55 yields/query. Same with DEFK_SLICE_US=10000000 (0.2-0.4 yields/query): +3.6-4.7%, so the yields are free. The pre-cut-off kernel (49637b5^) on today's compiler: -1.6..-3.4% (yielding faster), as in defk-nua -> no compiler regression to bisect; the +4% came with defk-8i4's reduce_while row loop: per-row safepoint (row loop holds the DP loop, no strips), resume check, strip copy of the DP loop (defk-w8l class). 27-28 vs 21 ms was load noise. Loadgen x3 (another session's mix ci overlapped 4 earlier runs; discarded): elixir 126-130 req/s, defk 652-663, blocking 676-693; /health p99 9.6-12.1 / 9.8-11.7 / 75-82 ms. Docs: fuzzy_search README, examples/README row, performance.md 1.6 + 6.4, 8.2 open question removed.

title: Re-measure fuzzy_search: defk 27 ms vs 21 ms blocking
